title: Deployment Conductor — Weekly Rotation & Incident Snapshot (Mar 9–11, 2026)
content:
Meeting: Deployment Conductor — weekly sync + hotfix routing dry run
Date/time: 2026-03-09 09:30–10:30 PST (notes updated 2026-03-11)
Owners / rotation this week:
  - Primary conductor: Ethan Morales (on-call rotation: week A)
  - Secondary conductor: Priya Nair (escalation)
  - Release infra SME: Marcus Li
  - Network / edge: Tomoko Sato
  - SRE liaison: Asha Raman

Attendees (live + async): Ethan, Priya, Marcus, Asha, Tomoko, Sofia (joined 20m), 2 rota observers

Quick summary / purpose:
  - Triage recent kernel-driver regressions impacting Dedicated nodes (see RD-4821). Confirm hotfix routing rules and a temporary unlock plan for capacity-constrained pools.
  - Run a dry-run of the new hotfix-routing playbook across the east/west release slots and validate preflight checks.
  - Capture decisions for rollback criteria and automated fallback thresholds for streaming endpoints.

Incident snapshot (kernel-driver regressions):
  - Symptom: degraded throughput on dedicated-gpu-pool-2 during large-batch workloads; increased tail latency (p95 -> 1.1s).
  - Timeline: first alert 2026-03-08 22:40 UTC; initial mitigation applied 2026-03-08 23:05 (drain + scale-down); investigation started 2026-03-08 23:20.
  - Root-cause hypothesis: new NV driver shipped in recent infra image triggered slower DMA path for medium-sized tensors; reproducible under synthetic load (Marcus repro script).
  - Impact: 3% of customer traffic routed through Dedicated pools experienced token-level latency spikes; no data loss.

Decisions made:
  1) Temporary routing override: divert new low-priority batch jobs to shared-hosted pools for 48 hours while kernel patch is tested on a canary set (canary window: 03-10 02:00–06:00 UTC).
  2) Hotfix channel: prioritize RD-4821 (kernel-driver revert) and open RD-4870 for backport to the 2.4.1 infra image.
  3) Rollback criteria (explicit): if p95 latency on any dedicated pool > 900ms for 15 continuous minutes OR error-rate for streaming endpoints > 0.8% for 10 minutes then initiate automated rollback to previous image and trigger post-mortem.
  4) Enable temporary permissive fallback for model-variant routing: allow model-variant downgrade for latency-sensitive endpoints when fallback improves p95 by > 20% during the canary.

Dry-run notes: hotfix-routing playbook v1.3
  - Step 0: preflight checks (disk, driver, node-health) — all green for canary nodes except one node with pending kernel-update label (Tomoko to reconcile).
  - Step 1: pause scheduled non-critical deploys across east-west release slots for 3 hours around canary window (PRIORITY: reduce noise).
  - Step 2: execute canary patch on 3 nodes (two AZs) — monitor kernel logs + perf metrics at 30s cadence.
  - Step 3: validate KV cache correctness + token continuity for live sessions (SLO samples from Customer A and internal synthetic harness).
  - Step 4: if validation passes, expand to 20% of dedicated pool traffic; if fails, run rollback per criteria.

Operational runbook additions (agreed edits):
  - Add explicit SLA for canary monitoring: telemetry retention for canary should be kept at 1s sampling for first 10 minutes, 10s afterward.
  - Add owner field to each runbook step (explicit person + backup).
  - Record an abbreviated 'decision sentence' at the top of the runbook for quick on-call consumption.

Capacity and release slots (matrix notes):
  - Current reserved capacity: dedicated-gpu-pool-1 (stable) 45 GPUs, dedicated-gpu-pool-2 (impacted) 40 GPUs; contingency pools available: 12 GPUs (burst).
  - Release slots this week:
      * Slot A (Mon 00:00–06:00 UTC) — maintenance window; low-latency releases permitted
      * Slot B (Wed 18:00–23:00 UTC) — high-throughput batch window (PAUSE for canary)
      * Slot C (Fri 01:00–05:00 UTC) — reserved for emergency hotfixes
  - Action: block Slot B for non-critical batch jobs for 3 days (Priya to notify scheduler).

Risk register (top 3):
  - R1: fallback to hosted pools increases per-token cost for affected customers (estimate +12% unit cost) — Finance notify required for significant customers.
  - R2: potential for stateful sessions to see a short reconnect during routing override — product to confirm acceptable behavior for affected customers.
  - R3: edge-case where canary sampling underrepresents peak due to time-zone alignment; mitigation: pick canary nodes in both US and EU AZs.

Action items (owner — ETA):
  - Marcus Li — finalize repro script and produce perf dashboard snippet for RD-4821 (2026-03-10 11:00)
  - Tomoko Sato — reconcile nodes with pending kernel-update label and mark them excluded from canary (2026-03-09 EOD)
  - Priya Nair — notify batch scheduler and cancel non-critical jobs in Slot B (2026-03-09 17:00)
  - Asha Raman — wire up 1s-sampling telemetry for canary metric set and create alert rule tied to rollback thresholds (2026-03-10 01:00)
  - Ethan Morales — run dry-run and lead canary; coordinate post-canary decision call (2026-03-10 02:00–06:00 UTC)
  - Sofia Patel — draft customer-facing incident note if canary expands (template ready) (2026-03-10 08:00)

Open questions / notes-to-self:
  - How to best communicate potential +cost impact to committed Dedicated customers without alarming them? (sales + CS sync needed)
  - Consider a short-term discount offer for customers hit by fallback routing (options? finance + legal)
  - Evaluate whether automated model-variant downgrade can be made opt-in per-customer as a durable feature (product + privacy implications)

Follow-ups / next meeting:
  - Post-canary decision call scheduled 2026-03-10 07:30 UTC (30m) — attendees: conductor + infra SME + SRE + product lead.
  - Next weekly conductor sync: 2026-03-16 09:30 PST.

Appendix (short logs & links):
  - Perf repro gist (internal): gist:marcus/repro-2026-03-08 (see linked artifact PR for details)
  - Quick checklist added to runbook: preflight -> canary -> expand -> rollback -> customer-comms

Informal notes / shorthand captured in meeting:
  - "if p95 > 900ms -> auto-rollback" (agreed)
  - "prefer fallback to hosted rather than throttling important customers" (debated)
  - "ensure decision sentence visible in Slack ops room"

End of notes.

(Author: Ethan Morales — put this up as the working doc; will convert to finalized runbook edits after the canary and post-mortem.)
